instruction.text: You are listening to an expert panel on the radio. What topic is being discussed? Select from the options.
instruction.sound: You are listening to an expert panel on the radio. What topic is being discussed? Select from the options.

atoms.a: Good afternoon everyone and thanks for tuning in today for our well-loved program 'A glimpse into the future'. I'm your host Andrea Goldsmith and today our expert panel will discuss the future of our cities in terms of urban architecture, living in harmony with the environment and possible new concepts of transportation. We have an expert in each field here in the studio with me today...

instruction.text: Who is the host talking to? Listen and choose the correct person.

atoms.a: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f10Us_chirp'>A warm welcome to our first guest. Thank you for being here today!</voice>. Thanks for having me! I've been looking forward to doing this programme! <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f10Us_chirp'>That's nice to hear! Please, tell us about yourself and your expertise in the field of urban development.</voice> Yeah, so I'm not an urban planner but my field is definitely involved in some of the planning that goes into the development of new urban spaces, I mean we do need buildings right? So when I say I design new building concepts, you can probably guess my profession.

instruction.text: Tick the statement that best reflects what is said by Malika. Only one answer is correct.
instruction.sound: Tick the statement that best reflects what is said by Malika. Only one answer is correct.

atoms.sound: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f10Us_chirp'>As an architect, what do you think the future of the buildings in our cities looks like?</voice>. Personally, I think it would do us all some good to perceive our analogue environment more in this age of online-everything, and the buildings we live in and see every day can seriously provide assistance. I believe that urban buildings need to feel less enclosed or like towering above you. More natural materials like wood or stone and definitely more natural light getting into the buildings wherever possible would create a new urban feeling. However, I am aware that the biggest task is to create enough affordable and liveable housing. <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f10Us_chirp'>Thank you for your insight. Now, what is everyone else's take on the matter?</voice>

atoms.a: Malika said that future buildings should...
b: ++ connect us to our analogue environment.

instruction.text: Match each opinion with the corresponding speaker.

atoms.a: Addressing the citizen's concerns is most important.

b.sound: I like the idea of designing buildings in order to benefit the people living in the city. As a public administrator I know that it's a tough legal and social process also with regard to funding. Essentially, what it really needs is a strategy that mainly considers the citizen's needs, but that's realistic in terms of implementation and budget as well.

atoms.a: Environmental challenges need to be taken into account.

b.sound: Natural materials are great, as long as they are sustainable. We need to think much further though and implement car free cities or at least car-free zones because natural materials and planting a few trees here and there is not going to solve the catastrophic impact city-life has on the environment and at the same time on its citizens.

atoms.a: The cities of the future will bring people closer together again.

b.sound: I think 'a new urban feeling' is a great goal and architecture is totally a part of it. However, I believe we actually need to consider architecture as a later step. First we will need to consider shared urban spaces like gardens or water installations, that help keep the air clean and revive a sense of community. Generally speaking, shared spaces need to regain importance!
